questions.title: At Least One Success via Complement

parts.text: A seed germinates with probability $0.28$, independently of other seeds. Six seeds are planted. Find the probability that at least one seed germinates, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Finding the Smallest Number of Trials

parts.text: A customer buys a product with probability $0.30$. Find the smallest integer $n$ for which the probability that at least one of $n$ independent customers buys the product is greater than $0.98$.
A spinner lands on blue with probability $0.20$. The spinner is spun until blue appears. Find the probability that blue first appears in fewer than 6 spins.

A machine produces a defective item with probability $0.22$. Nine items are inspected independently. Let $X$ be the number of defective items. Find the probability that more than 2 items are defective, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Strict Binomial Range Excluding Both Endpoints

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(10, 0.25)$. Find $P(4 < X < 8)$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Deriving Success Probability Before Binomial Complement

parts.text: A fair 6-sided die is rolled 8 times. Find the probability that a score of at least 5 occurs on at least 3 rolls, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: At Least One Success and High-Reliability Threshold

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(7, 0.4)$. Find the probability that $X \ge 1$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Find the smallest number of trials $n$ such that the probability of at least one success in $n$ independent trials is greater than $0.999$.

questions.title: Low-Probability Event and Sample Size Threshold

parts.text: A component in a high-voltage circuit has a probability of failing of $0.05$. An apparatus contains 8 of these components operating independently. Find the probability that at least one component fails, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
An engineer requires that the probability of at least one component failing in the apparatus is greater than $0.90$. Find the minimum number of components $n$ that must be tested.

questions.title: Strict Lower Bound and Complement Tail in Eleven Trials

parts.text: A delivery van is delayed with probability $0.15$, independently on each trip. A logistics supervisor checks 11 trips. Let $X$ be the number of delayed trips. Find the probability that fewer than 3 trips are delayed, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Hence find the probability that at least 3 trips are delayed.

questions.title: Target Practice: Upper Tail and Middle Range

parts.text: A marksman hits the bullseye with probability $0.35$ on each shot, independently of all other shots. The marksman fires 8 shots. Let $X$ be the number of bullseyes hit. Find the probability that the marksman hits more than 2 bullseyes, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Find the probability that between 3 and 5 bullseyes inclusive are hit.

questions.title: First Success Before Limit and Iterated Trial Threshold

parts.text: In a board game, a special spinner lands on red with probability $0.25$. A player spins the spinner repeatedly until red appears. Find the probability that red first appears in fewer than 5 spins, giving your answer as an exact fraction or decimal.

A player wins a round if red first appears in fewer than 5 spins. In a competition involving $N$ independent rounds, find the smallest value of $N$ such that the probability of winning at least one round is greater than $0.95$.

questions.title: Two-Tier Binomial: Weekly Puzzle Successes and Multi-Week Assessment

parts.text: A student solves a daily chess puzzle with probability $0.70$, independently each day. A study week consists of 5 days. Let $X$ be the number of puzzles solved in a week. Find the probability that the student solves at most 3 puzzles in a week, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Over a period of 8 independent weeks, let $Y$ be the number of weeks in which the student solves at most 3 puzzles. Find the probability that this happens in exactly 2 of the 8 weeks.
Find the probability that the student solves at most 3 puzzles in at least 3 of the 8 weeks.

questions.title: Quality Inspection: Multi-Box Shipping and Conditional Rejection

parts.text: In a factory, items are manufactured with a $12\%$ defect rate, independently of one another. An inspector takes a random sample of 10 items from a batch. A batch is rejected if more than 1 item in the sample is defective. Show that the probability of a batch being rejected is $0.342$, correct to 3 significant figures.

The factory inspects 12 batches independently. Let $Z$ be the number of rejected batches. Find the probability that at most 2 batches are rejected, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Given that at least one batch is rejected, find the conditional probability that exactly 2 batches are rejected.
